en: And that really is it for this app. Again,
if you wanna dive in deeper, the source code
was attached earlier in this section and you
can dive in deeper.
We, for example, also have a migrate script
which runs database migrations once to
populate the database and ensure that all
the tables are set up properly. And of
course, you can take a close look at all the
routes you find in there.
I went through all the key features and all
the core Bun APIs we're using here though.
And the only thing remaining therefore is
the test folder because Bun of course has
not just package management capabilities and
of course its runtime, but instead it also
has a built-in test runner. And I'm using
that too in this demo project here.
I got a bunch of test files here
and of course I got a test script where I
use the Bun test runner to run those tests.
First load the setup.ts file here and then
execute all these tests because the Bun test
runner will automatically look for files
that end with.test,
.ts,
.js, and so on.
In setup.ts, I simply set up a testing
database so that we
run those tests using a dedicated database
and not the production database, of course.
And then in those test files, I got various
tests for checking whether the upload logic
is correct, resigned URLs are created, if my
posts are loaded correctly, and so on and so
forth.
A bunch of tests, and all these tests are
built using just Bun features. So just
features from the Bun test runner
subpackage, so to say, for defining tests,
for running assertions and checking
conditions. So no external testing framework
or library is used
And of course, again, you can explore all
these tests here in depth. This of course is
not a testing course, but it's worth noting
that
just as the main app, this is all built
without any extra packages or libraries,
just using features built into Bun. So the
only exception for this overall app is
really BetterAuth, which simplifies the
process of setting up authentication.
